latin.523: §. VIII. Ad QUARTI SECULI Testimonia excutienda pedem promoturus, non possum non meminisse primo omnium locô præstantissimi hujusmodi Testimoniorum complexûs, PATRUM NICÆNORUM verbis concepti, totiusque Ecclesiæ ejus temporis christianæ de S. cœna sententiam aperientis; tantóque magis meminisse, quantò certiùs Formulæ administrandi Cœnam S., in Ecclesiis nostris Reformatis Marchicis aliisque receptæ, verba, administrationem ipsam immediatè antecedentia, complexui isti accepta ferenda videntur, quibus nempe Communicantes admonentur, cogitationibus suis non usque adeò Symbolis Sacris, in S. Cœna sensibus evidentissimè expositis, inhærere, sed verò oculos mentis in Cœlum dirigere, certòque certiùs, quin fide divina, statuere atque tenere, animas suas non minus ipso corpore sanguineque Christi veris ac substantialibus, saginari, quàm Symbola S. ore corporis à se assumantur ac percipiantur.
latin.524: Sic enim verba Nicænorum habent: Ne, inquiunt, proposito pani & poculo humiliter intenti simus, sed sublatâ in altum mente per fidem consideremus, proponi in S. illa Mensa Agnum Dei tollentem peccata mundi, & pretiosum ejus corpus & Sanguinem verè accipientes, nos credamus, hæc esse nostræ Resurrectionis (puta ad vitam æternam) symbola: Nam ideo etiam non multum, sed parum accipimus, ut agnoscamus, quod non ad satietatem, sed ad sanctificationem, accipiamus. Vid. Acta à Gelasio Cyziceno conscripta & ab Abrahamo Sculteto edita, Concilii vestigiis hisce exactissime insistit Catholicorum Patrum ac Theologorum Orthodoxorum omnium facilè princeps S. ATHANASIUS.
latin.525: Utpote adstruendis Spiritualibus præsentiâ ac participatione corporis & sanguinis Christi in S. Cœna, exclusis præsentia & participatione corporalibus, Commentario ad sextum Joh. caput, totus occupatus: Dominus, inquit, Spiritum à carne discriminavit, ut discerneremus ea, quæ loqueretur, non carnalia esse, sed spiritualia: Quod enim hominibus corpus ejus suffecisset ad cibum, ut universi mundi alimonia fieret? Sed proptereà adscensionis suæ in cælum mentionem fecit, ut eos à corporali intellectu abstraheret ac deinde carnem suam, de qua locutus erat, cibum è supernis cælestem & spiritualem alimoniam (pneumatikēn trophēn) ab ipso donandam intelligerent.
latin.526: Quæ enim, inquit, locutus sum vobis, Spiritus & vita sunt, quod perinde est ac si diceret corpus meum, quod ostenditur ac datur pro mundo, in cibum dabitur, ut spiritualiter (pneumatikōs) unicuique tribuatur & fiat singulis præservatio ad resurrectionem vitæ æternæ.
latin.527: Athanasio adstipulatur Rhetorum Sacrorum, circa exitum ejus Seculi, disertissimus, videl. S. AMBROSIUS, mutationem omnem quæ in symbola S. Cœnæ, per consecrationem eorum, competit, nonnisi spiritualem esse indigitans, Lib. 4. de Sacram. cap. 4. Tu ipse, inquit, eras, sed Vetus Creatura, postquam consecratus es, nova creatura esse cœpisti. Et iterum: Tu fortè dices, panis meus usitatus est; sed panis iste panis est, ante verba benedictionis sacramentorum, ubi accesserit consecratio, de pane fit corpus Christi.
latin.528: Hoc igitur adstruemus, quomodo qui panis est, potest esse corpus Christi consecratione. Consecratio autem fit verbis Domini, ut venerabile Sacramentum conficiatur. Vides quàm operatorius sit sermo Christi. Si ergo tanta vis est in sermone Domini, ut inciperent esse, (panis & vinum) quæ non erant, & in aliud commutentur, Ergo, ut Tibi respondeam, non erat corpus Christi ante consecrationem, sed post consecrationem jam est corpus Christi. Ipse dixit & factum est; TU IPSE ERAS, SED ERAS VETUS CREATURA; POSTQUAM CONSECRATUS ES, NOVA CREATURA ESSE CŒPISTI.

pass_a.523: §. VIII. About to advance my foot to examine the Testimonies of the FOURTH age, I cannot but remember first of all that most excellent complexus of Testimonies of this kind, conceived in the words of the NICENE FATHERS, opening the sentence of the whole Christian Church of that time concerning the Sacred supper; and so much the more to remember, the more certainly the words of the Formula of administering the Sacred Supper received in our Reformed Marchic Churches and others, immediately preceding the administration itself, seem to be owed to that complexus — by which Communicants are admonished not so far to cling in their thoughts to the Sacred Symbols most evidently set before the senses in the Sacred Supper, but truly to direct the eyes of the mind to Heaven, and surely and more surely, nay by divine faith, to establish and hold that their souls are no less fattened by the very true and substantial body and blood of Christ than the Sacred Symbols are assumed and perceived by the mouth of the body.
pass_a.524: For so the Nicene words have it: Let us not, they say, be humbly intent on the bread and cup set forth, but with mind lifted on high through faith let us consider that on that Sacred Table is set forth the Lamb of God taking away the sins of the world, and truly receiving His precious body and Blood, let us believe these are the symbols of our Resurrection (namely unto eternal life): For therefore also we receive not much but little, that we may acknowledge that we receive not unto satiety but unto sanctification. See the Acts written by Gelasius of Cyzicus and edited by Abraham Scultetus — in these footprints of the Council the easily foremost of all Catholic Fathers and Orthodox Theologians, S. ATHANASIUS, most exactly insists.
pass_a.525: As wholly occupied in the Commentary on the sixth chapter of John with establishing the Spiritual presence and participation of Christ’s body and blood in the Sacred Supper, the corporal presence and participation excluded: The Lord, he says, discriminated Spirit from flesh, that we might discern that the things He spoke were not carnal but spiritual: For how would His body have sufficed men for food, that it should become nourishment of the whole world? But therefore He made mention of His ascent into heaven, that He might draw them from corporal intellect and thereafter they might understand His flesh of which He had spoken as food from above, heavenly and spiritual nourishment (pneumatikēn trophēn) to be given by Himself.
pass_a.526: For the things, he says, that I have spoken to you are Spirit and life — which is as if He said my body, which is shown and given for the world, will be given for food, that it may be distributed to each spiritually (pneumatikōs) and become for each a preservation unto the resurrection of eternal life.
pass_a.527: To Athanasius agrees the most eloquent of Sacred Rhetors toward the end of that age, namely S. AMBROSE, indicating that every mutation which belongs to the symbols of the Sacred Supper through their consecration is only spiritual, Book 4 On the Sacraments ch. 4. You yourself, he says, were, but an Old Creature; after you have been consecrated, you have begun to be a new creature. And again: You will perhaps say, my bread is ordinary; but this bread is bread before the words of the blessing of the sacraments; when consecration has come, from bread is made the body of Christ.
pass_a.528: This therefore we will establish — how that which is bread can be the body of Christ by consecration. But consecration is made by the words of the Lord, that the venerable Sacrament may be confected. You see how operative Christ’s speech is. If therefore there is such force in the Lord’s speech that (bread and wine) begin to be what they were not, and are changed into another, Therefore, that I may answer you, it was not the body of Christ before consecration, but after consecration it now is the body of Christ. He Himself spoke and it was done; YOU YOURSELF WERE, BUT YOU WERE AN OLD CREATURE; AFTER YOU HAVE BEEN CONSECRATED, YOU HAVE BEGUN TO BE A NEW CREATURE.

523: §.VIII: stepping into the FOURTH century, first remember the Nicene Fathers’ complexus — opening the whole Church’s sentence on the Sacred Supper.

Our Marchic Reformed administration formula seems drawn from it: communicants must not cling to the sensed symbols, but lift the mind’s eyes to heaven and by divine faith hold that souls are fed by Christ’s true substantial body and blood no less than the mouth takes the symbols.
524: Nicene words (Gelasius of Cyzicus / Scultetus): do not stay humble-eyed on the set bread and cup — by faith see the Lamb of God on that Table, truly receiving His precious body and Blood as symbols of our resurrection unto eternal life.
We take little, not much — not for satiety but for sanctification. Athanasius most exactly follows these Council footprints.
525: Athanasius (on John 6) builds spiritual presence and participation of body and blood in the Supper — corporal presence and participation shut out.
The Lord separated Spirit from flesh so we know His speech is spiritual not carnal; He named the ascension to pull them off corporal intellect toward heavenly spiritual food (pneumatikēn trophēn).
526: ‘What I have spoken to you are Spirit and life’ — as if to say: my body shown and given for the world will be given as food so it is distributed to each spiritually (pneumatikōs).
It becomes for each a preservation unto the resurrection of eternal life.
527: Ambrose (De Sacr. 4.4), late in the century, agrees: every change that consecration works in the Supper’s symbols is only spiritual.
You yourself were an old creature; after consecration you begin to be a new one. Ordinary bread before the blessing-words; when consecration comes, from bread is made Christ’s body.
528: How can what is bread be Christ’s body by consecration? By the Lord’s words the sacrament is made — Christ’s speech is operative.

If bread and wine begin to be what they were not and are changed into another, then it was not Christ’s body before consecration, but after it is. He spoke and it was done: you were an old creature; after consecration you begin to be a new one.
Stop before §.IX (fifth century: Chrysostom and Augustine).
